source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which findings are typical of a pleural effusion?
questions.rationale: A pleural effusion (fluid in the pleural space) usually causes dyspnea on exertion and a dry, nonproductive cough from bronchial irritation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q227 (PDF p. 382)
questions.quote: Typical assessment findings in the client with a pleural effusion include dyspnea, which usually occurs with exertion, and a dry, nonproductive cough.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Lando, 70, is admitted with pneumonia. He has crackles, a productive cough, and dyspnea on exertion.
questions.stem: When is the SAFEST time to take Mang Lando for a short walk?
questions.rationale: Activities are scheduled after respiratory treatments. After a bronchodilator he has his best oxygen exchange and tolerates activity better. After meals he tires easily.
explanations: Breathing is not improved by a nap.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q231 (PDF p. 386)
questions.quote: The nurse should schedule activities for the client with pneumonia after the client has received respiratory treatments or medications.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Lando, 70, is admitted with pneumonia. He has crackles, a productive cough, and dyspnea on exertion.
questions.stem: Mang Lando says food has lost its taste. What BEST improves his appetite?
questions.rationale: Expectorating sputum dulls taste, so oral hygiene before meals helps. Small, frequent meals are better because of dyspnea.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q385 (PDF p. 554)
questions.quote: To minimize this adverse effect, the nurse should provide oral hygiene before meals.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Lando, 70, is admitted with pneumonia. He has crackles, a productive cough, and dyspnea on exertion.
questions.stem: Mang Lando gets short of breath during activity. Which action promotes his safety?
questions.rationale: Monitoring vital signs and oxygen saturation before, during, and after activity shows how he tolerates it. Pursed-lip breathing helps.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1330 (PDF p. 1632)
questions.quote: The nurse monitors vital signs, including oxygen saturation, before, during, and after activity to gauge client response.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Lando, 70, is admitted with pneumonia. He has crackles, a productive cough, and dyspnea on exertion.
questions.stem: Which discharge statement by Mang Lando shows a need for MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Incentive spirometry and deep breathing continue for 6 to 8 weeks after discharge to keep the alveoli open and clear secretions.
explanations: Correct answer: keep using it for 6 to 8 weeks.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q761 (PDF p. 990)
questions.quote: Deep breathing and coughing exercises and the use of incentive spirometry should be practiced for 6 to 8 weeks

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After a sclerosing agent is injected through the chest tube for pleurodesis, what should the nurse do?
options: Have him cough and deep breathe
questions.rationale: The tube is clamped so the agent does not drain back out, and a repositioning schedule spreads it within the pleural space.
explanations: Correct: keeps the agent in place.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q234 (PDF p. 389)
questions.quote: After injection of the sclerosing agent, the chest tube is clamped to prevent the agent from draining back out of the pleural space.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which intervention BEST promotes comfort for a client with AIDS and Pneumocystis pneumonia?
options: Raise the head of the bed
questions.rationale: Clients with breathing difficulty are usually more comfortable with the head of the bed raised. The other options monitor function rather than provide comfort.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q237 (PDF p. 392)
questions.quote: Clients with respiratory difficulties are often more comfortable with the head of the bed elevated.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with empyema will have a bedside thoracentesis. What should be ready in case it is not effective?
questions.rationale: Empyema is pus in the pleural cavity. If the exudate is too thick for thoracentesis, a chest tube may be needed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q239 (PDF p. 394)
questions.quote: If the exudate is too thick for drainage via thoracentesis, the client may require placement of a chest tube

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with empyema is scheduled for decortication. Which fact should guide the nurse's emotional support?
options: He will be in severe pain for weeks
He'll be discharged the next day
Chest tubes may stay in a long time
questions.rationale: Chest tubes remain until the former pus-filled space is obliterated, which may take time and be discouraging.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1005 (PDF p. 1256)
questions.quote: the client will have chest tubes in place after surgery, and these must remain until the former pus-filled space is completely obliterated.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Romy, 66, a former jeepney driver who smoked for 40 years, has COPD.
questions.stem: Which action shows Mang Romy is doing pursed-lip breathing correctly?
questions.rationale: Prolonging exhalation through pursed lips reduces air trapping from narrowed airways.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q302 (PDF p. 465)
questions.quote: Prolonging expiration time reduces air trapping caused by airway narrowing that occurs in COPD.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Romy, 66, a former jeepney driver who smoked for 40 years, has COPD.
questions.stem: Mang Romy is at risk for carbon dioxide narcosis. Which oxygen flow rate should the nurse confirm?
questions.rationale: In CO2 narcosis, the drive to breathe comes from low oxygen. A low flow (2 to 3 L/min) avoids removing that stimulus.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q531 (PDF p. 729)
questions.quote: For these clients, the stimulus to breathe is a decreased arterial oxygen concentration.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Romy, 66, a former jeepney driver who smoked for 40 years, has COPD.
questions.stem: Mang Romy is admitted with an exacerbation. Which factor MOST likely contributed?
questions.rationale: Dehydration thickens secretions and makes coughing ineffective. Correcting dehydration and teaching coughing technique help limit exacerbations.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q749 (PDF p. 978)
questions.quote: The nurse assesses the client for contributing factors such as dehydration and a lack of knowledge of proper coughing techniques.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Romy, 66, a former jeepney driver who smoked for 40 years, has COPD.
questions.stem: Which statement by Mang Romy about nutrition needs correction?
questions.rationale: Large meals distend the abdomen and push up the diaphragm, hindering breathing. Resting before meals reduces fatigue, and gas-forming foods are limited.
explanations: Correct answer: large meals impair breathing.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q760 (PDF p. 989)
questions.quote: Large meals distend the abdomen and elevate the diaphragm, which may interfere with breathing

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Romy, 66, a former jeepney driver who smoked for 40 years, has COPD.
questions.stem: What should home teaching for Mang Romy MOST importantly aim to do?
questions.rationale: COPD is airflow obstruction. Improving oxygenation and minimizing carbon dioxide retention are the primary goals; the other options support them.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q798 (PDF p. 1028)
questions.quote: Improving oxygenation and minimizing carbon dioxide retention are the primary goals.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The home nurse finds a client with emphysema smoking. Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'I see you never went to the clinic.'
'Have you looked at ways to quit?'
questions.rationale: The nurse avoids judgment and explores adaptive strategies without being controlling, leaving the decision with the client.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q818 (PDF p. 1052)
questions.quote: The nurse who observes a maladaptive behavior in a client should not make judgmental comments

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with COPD has a respiratory rate of 35 and extreme dyspnea. Which concern is MOST appropriate?
questions.rationale: Speaking clearly requires an intact respiratory system. Extreme dyspnea is a physical alteration that impairs speech.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q964 (PDF p. 1211)
questions.quote: Extreme dyspnea is a physical alteration that affects speech.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client is anxious about her first home chest physiotherapy. Which fact should reassure her?
questions.rationale: CPT mobilizes and clears secretions so breathing is more effective. It does carry some risks.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q907 (PDF p. 1150)
questions.quote: CPT is an intervention to assist with mobilizing and clearing secretions to enhance more effective breathing.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client has had hoarseness for 8 weeks. Which disorder is he at risk for?
questions.rationale: Persistent hoarseness is a common early sign of laryngeal cancer. Eight weeks is too long for acute laryngitis. Risk factors include smoking and heavy alcohol use.
explanations: Too long for an acute problem.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q395 (PDF p. 565)
questions.quote: Hoarseness is a common early sign of laryngeal cancer

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Forty-eight hours after admission for pleurisy, the pleural friction rub is gone. What does this indicate?
questions.rationale: A friction rub is heard early, before fluid builds up. Once fluid accumulates, there is less friction and the rub disappears.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q397 (PDF p. 567)
questions.quote: Once fluid accumulates in the inflamed area, there is less friction between the visceral and parietal lung surfaces, and the pleural friction rub disappears.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which instruction promotes comfort for a client recovering from pleurisy?
options: Take as much pain medicine as possible
questions.rationale: Splinting the chest wall during coughing and deep breathing eases pain. Shallow breaths promote atelectasis.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q709 (PDF p. 931)
questions.quote: The client with pleurisy should splint the chest wall during coughing and deep breathing.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement shows a client understands how to prevent another pulmonary embolism?
options: 'I'll cross my legs to rest them.'
questions.rationale: Elastic stockings improve venous return. Adequate fluids prevent hypercoagulability, and periods of walking are mixed with sitting.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q645 (PDF p. 863)
questions.quote: The recurrence of pulmonary embolism can be minimized with the wearing of elastic or supportive hose

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client suddenly shows signs of pulmonary embolism. Which order should the nurse carry out FIRST?
questions.rationale: Hypoxemia is the immediate threat, so oxygen comes first. An IV line for emergency drugs and an ECG follow.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1323 (PDF p. 1625)
questions.quote: The client needs oxygen immediately because of hypoxemia

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which findings are typical of rib fractures?
questions.rationale: Fractured ribs hurt on inspiration and palpation. Respirations are shallow, with guarding of the area.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1328 (PDF p. 1630)
questions.quote: The client with fractured ribs typically has pain over the fracture site with inspiration and to palpation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which breathing findings does the nurse expect with flail chest?
questions.rationale: Flail chest causes obvious respiratory distress: severe dyspnea, cyanosis, and paradoxical chest movement, with shallow, rapid, grunting respirations.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1329 (PDF p. 1631)
questions.quote: The client has severe dyspnea and cyanosis accompanied by paradoxical chest movement.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with a sucking chest wound has an occlusive dressing and is anxious. What BEST relieves his anxiety?
questions.rationale: Staying eases his anxiety and lets the nurse watch for a tension pneumothorax, which the dressing could cause.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q987 (PDF p. 1236)
questions.quote: Staying with the client has a twofold benefit.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Continuous bubbling appears in the water-seal chamber of a chest drainage system. What is the likely cause?
questions.rationale: Continuous bubbling through inspiration and expiration means air is leaking into the system. A resolving pneumothorax causes intermittent bubbling.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1321 (PDF p. 1623)
questions.quote: Continuous bubbling in the water-seal chamber through both inspiration and expiration indicates that air is leaking into the system.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: The water-seal chamber fluid is below the 2-cm mark. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: The water seal must be at 2 cm to keep air from re-entering the pleural space. Water evaporates, so the nurse refills it.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1351 (PDF p. 1654)
questions.quote: The water-seal chamber should be filled to the 2-cm mark to provide an adequate water seal

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After chest tube removal, which statement shows a need for MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: The site dressing stays in place until the provider says it may be removed. Heavy lifting is avoided for 4 to 6 weeks.
explanations: Correct answer: keep the dressing on.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1383 (PDF p. 1686)
questions.quote: This is maintained in place until the primary health care provider says it may be removed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement before percutaneous IVC filter insertion shows a need for MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: The percutaneous approach uses local anesthesia. Complications are rare.
explanations: Correct answer: local anesthesia is used.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1283 (PDF p. 1583)
questions.quote: The percutaneous approach uses local anesthesia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which emotional reaction in a client with silicosis needs IMMEDIATE intervention?
questions.rationale: Suicidal ideation is not a normal reaction and warrants immediate intervention. Anxiety, depression, and ineffective coping are common reactions.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1373 (PDF p. 1676)
questions.quote: Suicidal ideation is not a normal emotional reaction with this condition.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Why is positive-pressure ventilation given during electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)?
questions.rationale: A short-acting muscle relaxant is given to prevent injury during the seizure, so ventilation is supported until it wears off, usually within 2 to 3 minutes.
explanations: Correct: the relaxant affects the breathing muscles.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1272 (PDF p. 1573)
questions.quote: The client receives positive pressure ventilation until the muscle relaxant is metabolized, usually within 2 to 3 minutes.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A sputum culture grows Mycobacterium tuberculosis. How should the nurse interpret this?
options: Needs a skin test to confirm
questions.rationale: Culturing M. tuberculosis from sputum or tissue confirms active TB. A skin test helps but does not confirm active disease.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q354 (PDF p. 522)
questions.quote: Culture of Mycobacterium tuberculosis from sputum or other body secretions or tissue confirms the diagnosis of active tuberculosis.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which findings suggest pulmonary tuberculosis?
questions.rationale: Pulmonary TB causes cough, anorexia and weight loss, fatigue, low-grade fever, chills, night sweats, dyspnea, hemoptysis, and chest pain.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1322 (PDF p. 1624)
questions.quote: The client with pulmonary tuberculosis generally has a productive or nonproductive cough, anorexia and weight loss, fatigue, low-grade fever

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client with newly diagnosed TB will be in respiratory isolation for 2 weeks. Which action BEST prevents psychosocial distress?
options: Tell staff not to touch him
Limit nurse visits to save masks
questions.rationale: Visitors and social contacts give positive stimulation, and touch helps the client feel socially acceptable. A client in respiratory isolation is in a private room.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q963 (PDF p. 1210)
questions.quote: The nurse should note whether the client has visitors and social contacts because the presence of others can offer positive stimulation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding relates to chronic sinusitis?
questions.rationale: Chronic sinusitis causes anosmia (loss of smell), chronic cough, nasal stuffiness, purulent discharge, and headache worse on waking.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q382 (PDF p. 551)
questions.quote: Chronic sinusitis is characterized by anosmia (loss of smell), a chronic cough resulting from nasal discharge
